status: Collection questions, not confirmed findings or outreach

questions.question: What authority is actually delegated for a named autonomous function?
questions.request: Public operating rule or acceptance protocol specifying task authorization, supervision, exception intervention, override and responsibility.
questions.wouldChange: Distinguish policy commitments from implemented authority boundaries.
questions.alternativeExplanation: Human-control language may coexist with extensive task automation; it does not specify continuous human input.

questions.question: Which external dependencies are present in the customer's actual configuration?
questions.request: Versioned hardware/software inventory, deployment architecture, license/support terms and evidence for substitution cost.
questions.wouldChange: Identify a concrete dependency and switching burden without treating nationality as a complete stack description.
questions.alternativeExplanation: A public research repository may not be the shipping controller; an optional processor is not installed in every model.

questions.question: How much human work remains per accepted task?
questions.request: Matched task, intervention and person-hour logs; separate training, commissioning, live control, recovery and fallback.
questions.wouldChange: Calculate bounded workflow economics and characterize the actual division of work.
questions.alternativeExplanation: Labor may move to integration or recovery rather than disappear; data-collection teleoperation does not imply live teleoperation.

questions.question: Does performance survive the stated operating envelope?
questions.request: Civilian field results with version, load/posture, temperature, duration, sensor configuration, failure counts and accepted outputs.
questions.wouldChange: Separate laboratory or peak capability from repeatable use under customer conditions.
questions.alternativeExplanation: A favorable demonstration may omit cooling, charging, difficult inputs or recovery time.

questions.question: Who creates and owns the integration that makes the workflow useful?
questions.request: Dated integrator/customer scope of work, interface responsibilities, acceptance criteria and support contract.
questions.wouldChange: Attribute value and recurring work across OEM, integrator, software provider and customer.
questions.alternativeExplanation: A successful deployment may depend on extensive site-specific engineering rather than a general-purpose model.

questions.question: What specific artifact or capability crossed the civil–military boundary?
questions.request: A public dated procurement, collaboration, acceptance or ownership record naming the organizations, version/artifact and role.
questions.wouldChange: Promote a technical-relevance hypothesis into a bounded relationship; operating capability still requires separate evidence.
questions.alternativeExplanation: Similar technologies or institutions may have no documented transfer relationship.

questions.question: Which claims are backed by a formal requirement and which by actual testing?
questions.request: Accessible requirement text and separate configuration-specific test/acceptance report; identify issuer, assessor and effective date.
questions.wouldChange: Distinguish an authoritative rule, a draft, a participant list and tested conformity.
questions.alternativeExplanation: A standard's existence or a company's drafting participation does not establish conformity.

questions.question: Do newer learned policies reduce adaptation and recovery work at a new site?
questions.request: Held-out task/site evaluation with adaptation data, training time, human recovery, compute configuration and pre/post release comparison.
questions.wouldChange: Connect model progress to deployment effort and accepted output.
questions.alternativeExplanation: A benchmark gain can depend on extra demonstrations, a different embodiment or compute unavailable in the deployed configuration.
